mustKnow.item: Core thesis: TSLA's risk/reward has improved. Robotaxi/FSD execution risk is falling while the value is unchanged, so it is 'more worth buying' (更加值得买入)

Grantham: warned on CNBC that the S&P could fall 75%; said in 2019 Tesla would fail within 2 years (it then rose 10x); accused Musk of hype-funding. Musk replied 'not a builder' and did not deny it. The creator agrees Grantham wasn't wrong about the model
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge drops Grantham, the S&P -75% call and the 10x.

mustKnow.item: Third-party target: $475 by end-2026 if Cybercab runs smoothly, attributed to Morgan Stanley at 114s and 'JPMorgan' (摩根大通) at 272s
mustKnow.note: Neither notes that the creator names two different banks. LeapEdge turns the target into the creator's own trade target.

mustKnow.item: Fleet: Tesla about 500+ in roughly a year vs Waymo 4,000 after 10 years (an 8x gap); Tesla growing 17% per week; 60-69 Cybercabs in Austin
mustKnow.note: LeapEdge conflates these: 'zero to nearly 70 units in Austin in just over a year'.

mustKnow.item: Cost: Cybercab under $20k (below a Model Y); Waymo's Jaguar build over 100k, cheaper with Zeekr but still needs lidar and HD maps
Flywheel in Austin (more cars, users, revenue, cars); Waymo 'cannot compete'
Waymo survives only through Google funding; the creator doubts Google ever gets a return or will fight Tesla (and draws a parallel to Meta)
SpaceX was valued at $400-500B pre-IPO while loss-making (infinite P/E), and Tesla trades at about 200x P/E: investors price long-dated risk
mustKnow.note: Ours drops the 'PE 200倍' reference for Tesla.

mustKnow.item: Price context: 2021 high about 402-420, now about 300s. Success probability is much higher but the price is not
Horizon and risk: whether long-term or 1-2 years for robotaxi upside, holders must bear the risk that robotaxi fails or slips past 2026
mustKnow.note: Ours puts the 1-2 year and long-term framing in k8 but leaves the call's horizon null. LeapEdge says 'long-term' only.

ours.text: k7: 'Musk countered by stating Grantham is a short-seller/investor rather than a builder'
ours.problem: Embellished. Musk only said Grantham is 'not a builder'; the short-seller framing is the creator's, about Enron.
Misattribution. This is Grantham's forecast, which the creator implicitly discredits. It shows as a sentiment row with no owner.
A historical anecdote treated as an instrument sentiment. Noise.

Morgan Stanley vs JPMorgan inconsistency not flagged

leapedge.text: tradeIdea target '475美元'; summary: 'positions the stock for substantial upside toward a $475 target by 2026'
leapedge.problem: Misattribution. $475 is a third-party bank target that depends on Cybercab running smoothly in 2026. It is presented as the creator's unconditional trade target.

leapedge.text: 'growing from zero to nearly 70 units in Austin in just over a year'
leapedge.problem: Conflates two figures: about 500+ total fleet in a year, and 69 Cybercabs in Austin.
Regulation is never mentioned. The risk is generic filler.
A mild inference. The creator says the price has not risen much, not that it is an entry point. Directionally consistent.

sentimentIssues: 特斯拉 appears 5 times, all bullish/long. Collapse them into one row with the strongest quote (300s, '更加值得买入').
Waymo avoid: Waymo is not listed, so the investable read-through is a GOOGL negative, which is shown inconsistently as both neutral and bearish.
S&P 500 bearish and Enron bearish are third-party or historical, not creator stances. Drop them or tag them as attributed to Grantham.
why: Both find the single TSLA long. LeapEdge looks more actionable (ticker, target, horizon), but its $475 'target' is a conditional third-party bank target presented as the creator's, which is a material error for a PM. Ours attributes the target correctly (k1, with its condition) and covers Grantham, SpaceX, costs and fleet numbers. Its call lacks a ticker, horizon and attributed levels, and the sentiment table is noisy.
recommendations: Attach third-party levels to the call as a separate field, e.g. thirdPartyTargets:[{source:'Morgan Stanley (also said JPMorgan at 272s)', value:'$475', by:'end-2026', condition:'Cybercab operating smoothly'}]. This keeps actionability without LeapEdge's misattribution.
Fill horizon from the creator's framing: here '1-2 years for robotaxi upside, or long-term holder' (85s-93s). Ours had it in k8 but left the call's horizon null.
Flag conflicting source attributions for the same number (Morgan Stanley vs JPMorgan) in brief.omissions. That is a useful omission, unlike the 's6: Proposed quantity withheld' boilerplate.
Filter tickerSentiment to instruments the creator holds a view on. Drop historical anecdotes (Enron) and other people's forecasts (Grantham on the S&P 500), or tag them owner=third_party.
Resolve Chinese names: 特斯拉→TSLA. Also map private companies to their listed parent for read-through (Waymo→GOOGL, marked as indirect).
